reasons: Claimed status is compliant and no redline or counterparty comment was proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited paragraphs (§1 access/cooperation for service delivery; §5 fees/payment) contain no examination, inspection, records or verification right in Kubient's favour, so there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access term that could fall below the fallback.

Absence of any audit right binding the Customer is at least as protective as the preferred position; classifying it as 'missing' would wrongly require inserting an audit obligation against our own party, so 'compliant' is the correct label.
The failed 'audit frequency limited' regex is expected heuristic noise where no audit clause exists and does not evidence a gap.
Rationale appropriately parks the Kubient-measured impressions / no customer-side verification point under the reporting rule to avoid double-flagging the same commercial term.
